name: Bryophyllum pinnatum
short: A review cautions the plant is reported toxic (bufadienolides), without human harm data. Overactive bladder: 20-woman trial, events like placebo; no serious reactions there or in a 49-woman study.
text: A 2024 review cautions that Bryophyllum pinnatum has been reported to possess toxicity attributed to the bufadienolides it contains, and says its safety profile remains ambiguous; the abstract gives no data on harm in people. In an 8-week placebo-controlled trial in 20 postmenopausal women with overactive bladder, the incidence of adverse events was similar in both groups and no serious adverse events occurred, and in a 3-week nonrandomised study (the abstract describes no comparison group) in 49 women with overactive bladder and night-time urination who took chewable tablets of the plant by mouth (the abstract describes tablets made from the leaf press juice only for earlier studies), no serious adverse drug reactions were reported. In pregnancy, an observational study of pregnant women treated for sleep problems (the abstract gives neither the number of women nor any infant outcomes) detected no serious adverse drug reactions over 2 weeks, and a retrospective study of 67 matched pairs of women in preterm labour given intravenous (infused) Bryophyllum pinnatum or beta-agonist medicines found fewer women with palpitations or breathlessness on Bryophyllum (34.3% versus 55.2%) and equal or better newborn outcomes; that study used an intravenous route, not tablets. No interaction data were found in the cited sources.
